lifeEvents: Your back hurts too much to work.
A pipe burst and flooded your home.
A long illness. The Ministry asks you to prove it is long by waiting.
An accident at work. The workplace is fine, thanks for asking.
Someone crashed into your parked car. They have filed a form saying it was your fault.
A storm took your roof. The Ministry has opened a ticket. You are number 9,000.
A hospital stay. The bill arrived before you did.
Your knee made a strange noise. A doctor confirmed the noise, for a fee.
A flood reached the second floor. The flood office was on the first floor.
A family member got sick, and you had to stop working to help.
Your teeth need expensive repairs. All of them. At once.
A kitchen fire. The smoke alarm would like you to know that it tried.
A sudden diagnosis. The Ministry asks you to fill in the form again, on the right paper.
Your landlord sold the building and the rent went up.

l1.P1: NO TAX WINS. The player with 160 coins says it is 'fair, actually.'
NO TAX. The Ministry saves on paperwork, loses on everything else.
NO TAX WINS. The average player is thrilled. The average player does not exist.
NO TAX. Everyone keeps what they got. Some got more than others.
l1.P2: SAFETY NET WINS. Nobody gets less than 40 coins.
NOBODY BELOW 40. The Ministry calls it 'a reasonable minimum.' The minimum calls it 'a start.'
SAFETY NET AT {t}% TAX. The poorest player can breathe a little.
SAFETY NET WINS. Tightrope walkers approve.
l1.P3: GAP LIMITED. The richest player is now only a bit richer, and has complained.
RICH-POOR GAP LIMITED TO 100 COINS. The Ministry measured it with a ruler.
GAP SHRINKS BY LAW. The gap says it feels smaller.
GAP LIMITED AT {t}% TAX. Everyone is a bit more equal. Nobody is sure if that is good.
l1.P4: HELP THE POOREST WINS. Everyone is equally disappointed. The Ministry calls it 'teamwork.'
POOREST PLAYER NOW SLIGHTLY LESS POOR. Tax hits {t}%. A lot of tax money got lost on the way.
HELP THE POOREST WINS. The Ministry orders a statue. The statue is taxed at {t}%.
HELP THE POOREST WINS. The poorest player is the richest poorest player in history.
l1.tie: It was a tie. A coin was flipped.
Tie vote. A coin was flipped. The coin had no comment.
Tie broken by a coin. The Ministry calls it 'democracy, sort of.'
A coin was flipped. Someone asked for best of three. Request denied.
l2.highTax: Players discover free time. The economy goes missing.
TAX AT {t}%. Hard work was seen leaving the country with a small suitcase.
HIGH TAXES. Record equality. Record napping.
{t}% TAX. Economists predict disaster, then ask for money to study it.
l2.lucky: {name} earns a fortune and thanks hard work. Luck was not thanked.
LUCKIEST PLAYER THANKS THEIR HUSTLE. Their luck says nothing.
{name} tops the income list. Luck was 'just a small part,' says {name}.
{name} gets rich. The Ministry is checking whether the dice worked hard too.
l2.zeroTax: NO TAX THIS ROUND. Ministry staff are paid in compliments.
NO SHARING. Everyone keeps what they earned, and what they were lucky to get.
NO TAX. The richest player gives a speech about how they did it alone.
ZERO TAX. The Ministry sells a chair to pay for lunch.
l2.normal: TAX SET AT {t}%. The middle voter is happy. Everyone else is the middle voter's problem.
MEDIUM TAX. People in the middle celebrate, but not too much.
{t}% TAX. The Ministry calls it 'balanced.' Nobody checked.
THE MIDDLE VOTE WINS AGAIN. The middle voter wishes to stay anonymous.
l3.exit: INSURANCE COMPANY CLOSES. It says its customers kept needing insurance.
INSURER LEAVES. It is now selling cryptocurrency.
NOBODY BOUGHT. The insurance company closes its doors.
NO MORE INSURANCE. Protection is no longer available.
l3.premiumUp: INSURANCE NOW COSTS {premium} COINS. The company blames 'the kind of people who buy insurance.'
PRICES UP. The insurance company says this year looks like last year, but worse.
INSURANCE GETS PRICIER. Healthy players decide they feel lucky.
PRICE UP. The insurance company thanks its customers, and now suspects them.
l3.mandatory: INSURANCE FOR EVERYONE. Everyone is covered. Everyone also pays.
COMPULSORY INSURANCE. The Ministry checked everyone's gym records personally.
EVERYONE COVERED. Healthy players complain, then trip on the stairs.
SHARED INSURANCE WORKS. Nobody can leave, so the price stays steady.
l3.manyEvents: {events} PLAYERS HAD BAD LUCK. The Ministry hires more staff to process the forms.
BAD ROUND. Players without insurance learn what it is for.
LOTS OF BAD LUCK. The Ministry reminds everyone that bad luck is not a choice.
MANY CLAIMS. The insurance office asks for a quieter disaster next time.
l3.quiet: QUIET ROUND. Nothing bad happened. The insurance company calls it 'a great year.'
NO BAD NEWS. Players without insurance feel very smart today.
CALM ROUND. The gym was busy. Some people even went.
NOTHING HAPPENED. People who paid for insurance wonder why. That is how insurance works.
l4.squareComplex: HireBot is surprised. It changes its belief by {delta}. It calls that 'a lot.'
A SQUARE GETS A GOOD JOB. HireBot checks itself for errors. No errors found.
OLD BELIEF WEAKENS. HireBot now thinks {pi} of Squares are skilled. A little higher than before.
HIREBOT HIRES A SQUARE. HireBot says it was always open to this.
l4.noSquare: NO SQUARES IN GOOD JOBS. HireBot reminds everyone it only looks at data.
HIREBOT REPORT: Squares are 'nothing special, statistically.' Squares are still not hired.
THE COMPUTER IS FAIR, says the computer. Squares say the results are not.
HIREBOT NOW THINKS {pi} OF SQUARES ARE SKILLED. It calls its data 'very convincing.' It made the data.
l4.policy_B: BLIND HIRING STARTS. HireBot wears a blindfold, but still remembers the averages.
HireBot can no longer see shapes. It says it feels free and confused.
BLIND HIRING. Everyone is now judged by the average of everyone.
SHAPES HIDDEN. HireBot asks if it can at least see colors. It cannot.
l4.policy_C: QUOTA ROUND. HireBot hires as it is told. It learns nothing, as it is told.
THE QUOTA WORKS. Squares get good jobs. But fewer people bother to train.
QUOTA FILLED. HireBot fills in a form saying it disagrees.
QUOTA IN PLACE. Squares get jobs either way, so training matters less.
l4.policy_D: CHEAPER CHILDCARE. The office printer no longer has to babysit.
CHILDCARE PAID FOR. Parents can work long hours with much less chaos.
LONG HOURS GET EASIER FOR PARENTS. Children eat fewer meals at the office.
CHILDCARE HELP STARTS. The kids are fine. The budget is mostly fine.
l5.passedDonations: RULES CHANGED. The Ministry confirms no money changed hands, except the money that changed hands.
CHANGE PASSES AFTER SOME GIFTS. The giver says the gifts and the vote are unrelated.
NEW RULES: {t}% TAX, MINIMUM {F}. The people who gave coins call it 'very democratic.'
CHANGE PASSES. The Ministry is looking into the snacks.
l5.passed: RULES CHANGED. Players find new principles now that they know their incomes.
CHANGE PASSES: TAX NOW {t}%, MINIMUM {F}. Some eyebrows go up.
THE RULES CHANGE. Everyone agrees the new rules are fairer. For them.
NEW DEAL REACHED. Nobody remembers what they said an hour ago.
l5.failed: ALL CHANGES FAIL. Needing two-thirds of the votes did its job.
THE ORIGINAL RULES SURVIVE. Just barely.
CHANGES REJECTED. The losers blame 'the system.' The system says hi.
NO CHANGE. The rules stay at {t}% tax, minimum {F}. Some players feel betrayed by their past selves.
l5.noAmendments: NOBODY SUGGESTED A CHANGE. Players are either very principled or very tired.
THE ORIGINAL RULES STAND. The Ministry suspects a printing error.
NOBODY CHANGES ANYTHING. The Ministry is confused, and a little moved.
RULES KEPT AS WRITTEN. Historians will call this 'unusual.'
l2.lucky.you: YOU EARN A FORTUNE and thank hard work. Luck was not thanked.
LUCKIEST PLAYER THANKS THEIR HUSTLE. It was you. Your luck says nothing.
YOU TOP THE INCOME LIST. Luck was 'just a small part,' you say.
YOU GET RICH. The Ministry is checking whether the dice worked hard too.
